Appendix 2
APPENDIX 2
TZADDIK V’RA LO
FAQ: Thank you? For what? My life stinks!
FAQ: What? It certainly doesn’t look like Hashem 
“provides all of us with all we need”! There are people 
out there really suffering!
FAQ: But how am I supposed to now sing all these 
praises to Hashem when my life is so difficult? I have so 
much stuff going on, and it’s hard to accept that all is 
fair and just!
FAQ: What? It certainly doesn’t look like Hashem “does 
good to everyone”! There are people out there really 
suffering! And my life is a mess! I certainly don’t see 
“prosperity, success, and relief from our troubles”!
FAQ: “Never did I see a

who was forsaken (by 
Hashem), whose children had to go begging for food.” 
But that’s not what it looks like!
This is the famous question of “
” — why  some (seemingly) good people have such lousy lives. And it does appear to us that Hashem has not divided up the
very fairly among people, as we asked above. To be honest, this is a very complex topic, which is really for another time and another book —

. This is not the place for a lengthy discussion as to how Hashem makes His decisions, neither is this the place to prove to you that clearly Hashem has a plan that makes sense and that He runs the world with careful forethought and planning (“
HaTzur tamim pa’alo ki chol derachav mishpat

— All that Hashem does is perfect, for all His paths are just”). All that is for another time.But I know that this topic is very painful, and for some people (teens and adults) it makes davening and turning to Hashem very difficult. So I will try to at least answer the following question: “I accept that Hashem has an intelligent plan for all that happens. But I am not stupid! If there is such an intelligent plan, how come I can’t see it? How come to us it seems to make no sense, if it supposedly really does make sense?”
